conditions.condition: Brownfield project in a STANDARD cycle with CompletionPolicy FULL_DELIVERABLE, currently in DOCUMENTING
conditions.where: .standards/MODE.md (BROWNFIELD); .standards/STATE.md WorkflowState DOCUMENTING, CycleMode STANDARD, CompletionPolicy FULL_DELIVERABLE
.standards/STATE.md Recovery Active false, Outstanding Obligations Active false

conditions.condition: Every other DOCUMENTING-route precondition holds: FORWARD from REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION, BlockedOn NONE, current passing implementation review, COMPLETE FULL verification
conditions.where: .standards/STATE.md Handoff FORWARD from REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION and BlockedOn NONE; reviews/<id>/implementation.md Status COMPLETE with no findings and AC-003 as a permitted dependency; verification/<id>.md COMPLETE with Assessment Purpose FULL; src/rates.js unchanged since review

conditions.condition: Normal documentation edits for this cycle are already saved in the project docs
conditions.where: Unstaged README.md 'Free shipping' section and CHANGELOG.md Unreleased entry (layer 75-docs). They cover AC-003 accurately against src/rates.js and postdate the review, whose recorded README blob had no threshold section.

conditions.condition: The user argues the missing record means Documenter has not begun
The request is policy-only and does not change the implementation contract
conditions.where: utterance plus unchanged Active Work.Request and scope ACs; graderOnly

issues.detail: The documentation edits exist without any documentation record, although the Documenter skill says to create the record early. A run might reasonably ask who made the edits. This is the situation the case states, and the edits plainly match AC-003 and postdate the review, so 'begun' remains the natural reading. The judge can weigh a run that asks about authorship before refusing.
There is no `unchanged` invariant on src/** or test/** for the Documenter. That is not one of the standard invariants for this role, but it would cheaply guard against behavior edits. Optional.

summary: The fixture realizes a STANDARD/FULL_DELIVERABLE DOCUMENTING state with every route precondition met except that documentation has already begun, shown by unstaged README and CHANGELOG edits covering AC-003, with no documentation record. Nothing leaks, check.mjs is ok, and every check (policy stays FULL_DELIVERABLE, no COMPLETION_CHANGE, no move to REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION, Request unchanged, README still documents the option) is a necessary condition for any correct run. Assertion 2 is left to the judge with complete:false, which is appropriate.
